name: Minutes - June 11, 2020 - Special Meeting
minutes_text:
Final Minutes Approved July 7, 2020
  MINUTES

  Special Meeting of the
  City of Huntington Park City Council
  Thursday, June 11, 2020

The City Council conducted this meeting in accordance with California Governor
Newsom's Executive Order N-25-20 and N-29-20.

The Rules of Decorum were played prior to the start of the Regular Meeting.

The special meeting of the City Council of the City of Huntington Park, California was
called to order at 5:04 p.m. on Thursday, June 11, 2020, in the Council Chambers at City
Hall, 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California; Mayor Manuel "Manny" Avila
presiding.

PRESENT: Council Member(s): Eduardo "Eddie" Martinez, Marilyn Sanabria, Karina
Macias, Vice Mayor Graciela Ortiz, and Mayor Manuel "Manny" Avila.

CITY OFFICIALS/STAFF: Ricardo Reyes, City Manager; Cosme Lozano, Chief of Police;
Araceli Almazan, Legal; Raul Alvarez, Assistant City Manager; Sergio lnfanzon, Director
of Community Development/Acting City Clerk; ABSENT: Cynthia Norzagaray, Director of
Parks & Recreation; Nita McKay, Director of Finance & Administrative Services; Cesar
Roldan, Director of Public Works.

INVOCATION

Invocation was led by Council Member Martinez.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Sanabria.

PUBLIC COMMENT -

A representative from the business "Dream Maker" talked about the importance of being
invited to all the council meetings. She stated that all the small businesses located on
Pacific Boulevard didn't have resources, and didn't receive any information about the help
from the city. She also requested help from the city with publicity and the information
about the loans. She stated that she was representing many of the small businesses and
that they have formed a group called united small business. She mentioned they were
struggling due to the COVID-19 situation and felt that they needed to be heard. The
representative asked to have a conference with all of the councilmembers so business
owners could share their concerns. The representative requested a letter from the city to
the landlords asking them to help them with their rent.

Alejandro Melendi (business owner) - Mr. Melendi mentioned that changing the name
from microbusiness to small business will affect those businesses that have less than 3
employees and all microbusiness will be affected. He also stated that 95% of those
microbusinesses haven't received any type of federal funding.

Yohanna Ruvalcaba (business owner) - She stated that she had a high rent and she
needed help from the City.

Gloria Rivera (business owner) - Miss Rivera stated that she applied to different loans
and didn't qualify because she only had one person on the payroll. She asked the city to
do more publicity so people know that they are open.

Chamber of Commerce (business owner) - Leticia Martinez mentioned that most of the
businesses in Huntington Park are microbusinesses and need help. She also stated that
she heard that out of the $250,000 allocated, only $50,000 were allocated for
administration, but then she saw that $25,000 are secured for administration so she asked
for a clarification to provide the exact amount available for the small business to apply.
She also mentioned that she doesn't understand why the loans will be used to stabilize
or expand current businesses, she didn't see how under the current economic times that
 would be possible. The Chamber of Commerce is asking council to consider keeping the
microloan vs including other businesses due to the unlimited amount of funds.

Ahmed Hassanin (business owner) - Mr. Hassanin stated that he has been in Huntington
Park for 20 years as a business owner and this has been the hardest moment. He stated
he was a microbusiness and needed help. He asked the Council to consider to keep the
loans for microbusinesses of less than 5 employees. He also stated that he would like to
come back and meet with the councilmembers and share some ideas about how to
improve the boulevard.

STAFF RESPONSE - Mr. Reyes stated that the item to be considered at the meeting
was the housing assistance program being developed by the City and not the small
businesses program. The microbusinesses are still eligible under the small business
program so they will not be left out. The City continues working on the small business
program to make it fair for everyone and once is ready the City will release the application.

Council Member Sanabria had a question about the eviction moratorium and Mr. Reyes
responded that the City under the emergency proclamation approved an eviction
moratorium for commercial and residential. He also stated that if anyone was experiencing
any formal eviction, to contact the Community Development Department for assistance.

Council Member Martinez asked if the eviction moratorium was until the end of June and
Mr. Reyes responded that the emergency proclamation didn't have an expiration date and
was going to continue until changes were made by Council.

Vice Mayor Ortiz stated that she was going to make comments or questions during the
public hearing or when the item in the agenda was under discussion by the City Council.

  REGULAR AGENDA

CITY MANAGER

1.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF SUBSTANTIAL AMENDMENT
  NUMBER THREE TO THE FY 2019-20 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN (AAP) FOR
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT CORONAVIRUS RESPONSE
  (CDBG-CV) FUNDS

City Manager announced the item and introduced Renea Ferrell to present the item.

Mayor Avila opened the public hearing:

PUBLIC COMMENT

Leticia Martinez (Chamber of Commerce) stated that there are 2000 businesses
registered in the City, and according to the presentation by Miss Renea only 20
businesses will be eligible for a $10,000 forgivable loan, she asked if there was any way
to change that so more businesses could get help. Limiting to 20 was not going to cut it
for all the small businesses you have in the City. She also asked why bringing the issue
about the small business description to Council to vote if the City was still working on it.

Alejandro Melendi (business owner) talked about the 20 loans being not enough for the
businesses in the City, he also asked the City Council to allocate funds from other sources
to help them.

Business Owner from June Maker talked about reducing the amount of the loan to help
more small businesses. She also stated that the businesses are interested in participating
and access the information for the meetings.

Joana Ruvalcaba (business owner) stated that every business pays different amount of
rent, therefore, one option to help the businesses is to allocate the amount of the loan
based on the amount of rent businesses pay.

Ahmed Hassanin (business owner) asked the City Council to help the small businesses.

  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
June 11, 2020  Page 2 of 4
  Vice Mayor Ortiz made a point of clarification and stated that they were not voting on the
 small business loan program. She clarified that the City Council was voting to modify the
 amount the Salvation Army was going to receive to manage the Homeless vouchers
 program, and adding to microenterprise the term small businesses and the CDBG
 administration amount. There are still concerns the City has to address and the City
 Council is not voting on the small business program but just to add the small business to
 the criteria.

 Mayor Avila closed the public hearing:

 Council Member Sanabria stated that Council is listening and working to help everyone
 in the City and at this point they are just voting on the homeless program and adding the
 small business component.

Motion: Vice Mayor Ortiz moved to approve the substantial amendment number three
to the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Annual Action Plan (AAP) for Community Development
Block Grant Coronavirus response (CDBG-CV), seconded by Council Member Sanabria.
Motion passed 5-0-0, by the following vote:

 ROLL CALL:

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martinez, Sanabria, Macias, Vice Mayor Ortiz
  and Mayor Avila
  NOES:  Council Member(s): None
  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

2.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF FIRST AMENDMENT TO LOCAL
  EMERGENCY PROCLAMATION

Assistant City Manager Raul Alvarez presented the item:

Motion: Council Member Sanabria moved to approve the first amendment to local
emergency proclamation, seconded by Vice Mayor Ortiz. Motion passed• 5-0-0, by the
following vote:

ROLL CALL:

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martinez, Sanabria, Macias, Vice Mayor Ortiz
  and Mayor Avila
  NOES:  Council Member(s): None
  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

  END OF REGULAR AGENDA

DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS

Acting City Clerk Sergio lnfanzon stated that a correction needed to be made and that
the local emergency eviction moratorium for the City of Huntington Park ended on May
31, 2020, however, the City was still abiding by the eviction moratorium from the Los
Angeles County that is in effect until the end of the month.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS - None.

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

Council Member Macias thanked Director lnfanzon, staff and business owners for
attending the meeting. She also stated that they try to divide the funds as much as
possible to help and provide resources. We understand the situation is difficult but we are
trying to help as much as possible.

  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES
June 11, 2020  Page 3 of 4
 Council Member Martinez thanked Director lnfanzon and acknowledged all the small
business attending the meeting today and encouraged everyone to participate and
continue voicing their concerns.

Council Member Sanabria thanked all the people who attended the meeting, asked
everyone to visit the City's website and get the latest information on the decisions the City
is making. She stated that Council is here to help and her business card is always
available. She also thanked Director lnfanzon for the good work he is doing. She
encouraged everyone to complete their census form and return it as soon as possible.

Vice Mayor Ortiz thanked the business owners and let them know that the Council
Members always listen to everyone. She stated that we are living a very difficult time and
there are different needs for everyone, not just the small businesses are in need of
financial assistance, there are families that are living in the streets and they need food,
and housing. She stated that small businesses are very important because they are the
foundation of our economic plan, but the reality is that the federal government didn't give
us what we needed, we have a small pot and we have to divide it for; housing, food, and
businesses. She also mentioned that her business card is available and invited the
attendees to call or email her to figure out what is realistic for the small businesses.

Mayor Avila thanked all businesses attending the meeting and mentioned that the City
Council is listening and if they have an opportunity to help them, they will do it. He also
encouraged everyone to continue participating.

ADJOURNMENT
Mayor Avila adjourned the meeting at 6:01 p.m. in the name of all the Class 2020
Graduates, to a Regular Meeting on Tuesday, June 16, 2020 at 6:00 P.M.

Respectfully submitted,
